_meta.title: EEOC job-discrimination cases announced in press releases
_meta.what: One point per US Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) press release that announces a lawsuit, settlement, consent decree, conciliation, jury verdict or court judgment against a named employer (or other respondent) for discrimination, harassment or retaliation at work, all years and all bases on eeoc.gov's newsroom (1994-2026). Releases not about a specific case (statistics, guidance, hearings, meetings, staff news, outreach), amicus-brief releases and subpoena-enforcement releases are left out, as are Spanish-language releases (eeoc.gov posts Spanish versions of English releases; they are counted in _meta.counts.left_out_by_reason) and media advisories. Releases that announce several employers at once are kept as one record (name as written, which may be a group description). A case announced in several releases (e.g. the suit and later the settlement) appears once per release. Releases posted twice on eeoc.gov with identical text are kept once (other URL in duplicate_urls). All fields are taken from the release text; points are placed at the US Census Gazetteer internal point of the city named in the release as the employer/workplace location ("City, State" in the text), otherwise the dateline city. Only the release lead (first two paragraphs) is searched for the employer/workplace city, and a person's home town is skipped. If the first place named there is not in the Gazetteer places file (e.g. a county, Long Island, an unincorporated area), the dateline city is used and geo_source says so. The dateline state comes from the dateline itself, else the EEOC office city it names, else a state named in the text. New York City boroughs are placed at the New York city point. Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands and American Samoa are not in the Gazetteer places file, so those records have no coordinates. Fields not stated in the release are null. Records with no matched city are kept with null lat/lon. Releases from before 2009 are few because eeoc.gov's newsroom carries few of them.
_meta.source: US Equal Employment Opportunity Commission press releases (US government work, public domain)
_meta.geocoder: US Census Bureau 2026 Gazetteer national places file (2026_Gaz_place_national.txt), https://www2.census.gov/geo/docs/maps-data/data/gazetteer/2026_Gazetteer/

fields.bases: normalised list: race, color, sex, pregnancy, sexual harassment, national origin, religion, age, disability, genetic information, equal pay, retaliation, sexual orientation/gender identity
fields.bases_text: basis words as they appear in the headline/lead of the release
fields.action: sued / settled / consent decree / conciliation / verdict / judgment
fields.geo_source: which city was used: text = "City, State" named in the release; dateline = release dateline city (with how its state was known)
fields.name_source: where the employer name was read: lead sentence, case caption (EEOC v. ...), or headline; "weak match" = a name found after against/with/sued in the lead that could not be cross-checked with the headline or caption
fields.case_caption_name: the defendant named in the case caption (EEOC v. ...), when the release gives one
fields.gazetteer_place: the Census Gazetteer place matched, with its GEOID
fields.duplicate_urls: other eeoc.gov URLs carrying the same release
